hints: Focus on what the fuel actually is, work out the molecular formula of methylpropan-1-ol first.
Write the balanced equation for complete combustion to CO2 and H2O, this alcohol is C4H10O and needs 6 mol of O2 per mole.
Convert moles of oxygen to volume at r.t.p. using 1 mol of gas occupies 24 dm3, then match to the options.
walkthrough:
**Find the formula of the alcohol**

Methylpropan-1-ol is propan-1-ol with an extra methyl group. That gives 4 carbons in total.

So the formula is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{OH}$, which is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$.

**Write the balanced combustion equation**

Complete combustion of a fuel containing C, H and O gives carbon dioxide and water only.

$$\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O} + 6\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 4\text{CO}_2 + 5\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Check it: 4 C on both sides, 10 H on both sides, and 1 + 12 = 13 O atoms on both sides. So 1.0 mol of alcohol needs 6.0 mol of $\text{O}_2$.

**Convert moles of oxygen to volume at r.t.p.**

At room temperature and pressure, 1 mol of any gas occupies $24 \text{ dm}^3$.

$$\text{volume} = \text{moles} \times 24 = 6.0 \times 24 = 144 \text{ dm}^3$$

options.A: 108 dm3 is 4.5 mol of O2. That is the correct volume for unsubstituted propan-1-ol, C3H8O. It is the trap if you forget the extra methyl group and balance C3H8O + 4.5O2.
options.B: 144 dm3 is correct. 1.0 mol of C4H10O needs 6.0 mol of O2, and 6.0 x 24 dm3 mol-1 = 144 dm3 at r.t.p.
options.C: 156 dm3 is 6.5 mol of O2. This comes from a balancing slip, for example miscounting H or O atoms when balancing the water and oxygen. Careful atom balance gives exactly 6 O2, not 6.5.
options.D: 288 dm3 is double the correct volume. It is 12 mol of O2, the trap if you double the equation or multiply by 2 by mistake, or confuse atoms of O with molecules of O2.
